en: Doctrines must necessarily, even when their authority rests on a divine revelation, be so constituted that they are really authorised by the general reason of men, that every man sees and feels their obligation as soon as he has been made attentive to it — for, besides that such doctrines, which promise either to indicate to us a particular means of obtaining God's good pleasure, or otherwise to procure for us some particular higher knowledge, closer disclosures about unattainable objects, and indeed for the sake of reason, not merely of the imagination — besides that they sooner or later become an object of attack by thinking men and an object of dispute, in which the practical interest is always lost, or on account of the dispute precise, intolerant symbols are set up, they will certainly, because their connection with the true needs and demands of reason always remains unnatural, and because they, even if this connection has nevertheless become quite firm through habit, easily give occasion to abuses, never attain in feeling the importance of a pure, genuine practical moment that relates immediately to morality.
zh: 这些学说，即使它们的权威建立在一种神圣的启示上，也必然要这样：它们其实是靠人的普遍理性才得到认可的，每个人只要注意到它们，就会看出并感到自己受它们约束——因为，除了这样一点：这类学说要么答应告诉我们一种特别的手段去赢得上帝的喜悦，要么答应给我们弄来某种别的高深知识、关于那些达不到的对象的更切近的说明，而且是为了理性、不只是为了想象力的缘故——除了它们早晚会成为有思想的人攻击的对象、成为争吵的对象（在争吵中，实际的好处总是丢掉了，或者因为争吵而订立出一些严格而不宽容的信条）之外，它们还一定会——因为它们跟理性的真正需要和要求的联系始终是不自然的，而即使这种联系靠习惯变得十分牢固，它们也容易招来各种滥用——永远无法在感受里取得那样一种重要性：一个纯粹的、真正的、直接关系到道德的实际环节所具有的重要性。

en: But these doctrines must also be simple, and if they are truths of reason, they are simple precisely for that reason, because they then need neither an apparatus of erudition nor an expenditure of laborious proofs: and through this property of being simple they will exercise all the more strength and emphasis on the mind, on the determination of the will to actions, and thus concentrated have far more influence, far more share in the formation of a spirit of a people, than when the commandments are heaped up, artificially ordered, and precisely for that reason always need many exceptions.
zh: 但这些学说也必须是简单的；如果它们是理性的真理，那它们正因此就是简单的，因为它们用不着博学的装备，也用不着费劲的证明：凭着这种简单，它们对人心、对意志下决心去行动，会发挥更大的力量和分量，而且这样集中起来，对一个民族精神的形成会有大得多的影响、大得多的份量，远胜过那些戒律堆成一堆、人为地排列起来、并正因此总需要许多例外。

en: These general doctrines must at the same time be human — a great and difficult demand — and indeed so human that they are suited to the intellectual culture and the level of morality on which a people stands.

Precisely some of the most sublime and for men most interesting ideas are hardly qualified to be generally adopted as maxims — they seem to be only the property of a few tested men who have penetrated to wisdom through long experience, in whom they have become firm faith, conviction not to be shaken precisely in the situations where it is supposed to raise one up.
Of this kind is especially the faith in a wise and kindly providence, with which, when it is living and of the right kind, complete submission to God is bound up.
zh: 这些普遍的学说同时必须是人性的——这是一个重大而艰难的要求——而且必须人性到这样的程度：它们要适合一个民族所处的精神教养和道德水平。
恰恰是那些最崇高、对人又最有意思的观念，恐怕很难有资格被普遍地当作准则接受下来——它们似乎只是少数经过考验、靠长期经验达到智慧的人的所有物；在这些人的心里，它们已经变成坚定的信仰，变成一种恰恰在需要它把人扶起来的时候也不会动摇的确信。
属于这一类的，特别是对一种智慧而仁慈的天意的信仰；这种信仰只要是活的、是正当的，就与对上帝的完全顺从连在一起。

en: However much this doctrine, and everything connected with it, is the chief doctrine in the Christian community, since everything that is set forth in it reduces itself to the unattainable love of God, into which everything runs out, and further, year in, year out, God is represented to us as always near and present, bringing about everything that goes on around us; however much this is represented not merely as standing in the most necessary connection with our morality and with what is holiest to us, but is also raised to the fullest certainty by frequent assurances of God himself, by other facts that are supposed to convince us of it irrefutably — we nevertheless see through experience, among the great crowd, that a thunderbolt, a cold night can make this trust in providence and patient submission to the will of God, which should follow from it, very faint-hearted; that it is altogether only the part of a wise man to rise above impatience, vexation over failed hopes, and ill humour over misfortunes.
zh: 这个学说，连同与它相关的一切，是基督教团体里的主要学说，因为其中所讲的一切都归结为上帝那高不可攀的爱，一切都归结到它；而且年复一年，我们得到这样的表象：上帝始终就在近旁、就在场，我们周围发生的一切都是他促成的；这个学说不仅被表象为与我们的道德、与对我们最神圣的东西处在最必然的联系之中，而且还凭上帝自己的多次保证、凭另外一些本应无可反驳地说服我们的事实，被抬高到最完满的确定性——尽管这样，我们还是从经验里看到，在普通大众身上，一声霹雳、一个寒夜就能使这种对天意的信赖和由此应当产生的对上帝意志的耐心顺从变得十分怯懦；看到能撇开不耐烦、对希望落空的恼怒、对不幸遭遇的闷闷不乐，根本只有明智的人才做得到。

en: That so sudden striking-down of trust in God, the quick transition to discontent with him, is made all the easier by the fact that the Christian mob is not only accustomed from youth on to pray incessantly, but one also always seeks to persuade them of the highest necessity of this by promising them a certain fulfilment of it.
zh: 对上帝的信任这样一下子被压垮，又这么快转成对他的不满，之所以更容易发生，是因为基督教里的群氓从小就被养成不停祈祷的习惯，而且还总是靠许给他们祈祷一定会有回应，来说服他们相信祈祷极其必要。

en: Further, for the benefit of suffering humanity, a heap of grounds of comfort to be used in misfortune has been scraped together from all ends and places, such that in the end one could feel sorry that one does not have to lose a father or mother every eight days, is not struck with blindness; reflection has here taken the course that with incredible acuteness physical and moral effects have been traced and reasoned out to the widest extent, and, by setting these up as purposes of providence, one believed thereby to have gained closer insights into its plans with men, not merely in general but also in detail.
zh: 此外，为了受苦的人类的好处，人们从四面八方搜罗来一大堆在不幸时用得上的安慰理由，多到最后一想到自己不是每隔八天就得失去一位父亲或母亲、没有瞎掉眼睛，反倒会觉得遗憾；在这里，思考走上了这样一条路：用令人难以置信的敏锐把物理的和道德的效果一直追到最远，绞尽脑汁把它们想出来，再把它们立为天意的目的，于是便以为自己由此对天意跟人打交道的计划有了更切近的了解，不只是在一般上，而且在个别事情上。

en: But as soon as we are not content, in this matter, to lay a finger on the mouth full of holy awe and fall silent, nothing is more common than that presumptuous forwardness takes it upon itself to want to master its ways too — a propensity which is strengthened, to be sure not among the common people, nor by the many idealistic ideas that are current.
All of which contributes little indeed to furthering submission to God's will and contentment.
It might be very interesting to compare the faith of the Greeks with this.

With them there lay at the basis, on the one hand, the faith that the gods are gracious to the good and deliver the evil over to terrible Nemesis — built on the deep moral need of reason, sweetly enlivened by the warm breath of feelings, not on the cold conviction deduced from individual cases that everything is turned to the best, which can never be brought into true life; on the other hand, misfortune with them was misfortune, pain was pain — what had happened and could not be changed, about its purposes they could not brood, for their μοῖρα, their ἀνάγκαια τύχη was blind; but to this necessity they then also submitted willingly with all possible resignation and had at least the advantage that one bears more easily what one has been accustomed from youth on to regard as necessary, and that misfortune, besides the pain, the suffering it gives birth to, does not also bring forth the far more burdensome — more unbearable — vexation, ill humour, discontent.

This faith, since it is respect for the stream of natural necessity on the one hand and at the same time the conviction that men are ruled by the gods according to moral laws, seems to be humanly suited to the sublimity of the Godhead and to the weakness, the dependence on nature and the limited horizon of man.
zh: 可是，只要我们在这件事上不甘于满怀神圣敬畏地用手指按住嘴、一声不响，那么最常见不过的就是：自以为是的好奇多事竟敢要把它的道路也来摆布一番；这种倾向虽然不是在下层民众那里、也不是靠那些流行的理想化观念得到加强的。
这一切对促进对上帝意志的顺从和知足，恰恰没有多少帮助。
把希腊人的信仰拿来跟这一套比较，也许会很有意思。

在他们那里，一方面是以这样一种信仰为根基的：神对好人慈爱，把坏人交给可怕的复仇女神去处置——这信仰建立在理性那深刻的道德需要上，被感受的温暖气息亲切地吹活，而不是建立在那种从个别事例推出来的、冷冰冰的确信上，即相信一切都会往最好处转，这种确信永远带不进真正的生命里去；另一方面，在他们那里不幸就是不幸，痛苦就是痛苦——已经发生、无法改变的事，他们不会去琢磨它的用意，因为他们的 μοῖρα、他们的 ἀνάγκαια τύχη 是瞎的；但他们对这种必然性也就心甘情愿地顺从，尽可能听天由命，而且至少有这么个好处：从小就习惯把一件事看作必然的，人就比较容易忍受它；不幸在它所生的痛苦、苦难之外，不会又添上那沉重得多、也难忍得多的恼怒、烦闷和不满。
这种信仰，一方面是对自然必然性之流的敬畏，同时又确信人是受神按道德法则统治的，所以它看来既合乎神性的崇高，也合乎人的软弱、对自然的依赖和狭隘的眼界。

en: Simple doctrines grounded on general reason agree with every degree of popular culture, and this culture will gradually modify those doctrines according to its changes too, though more as regards the outward work, more as regards what concerns the painting of the sensuous imagination.
zh: 简单的、建立在普遍理性上的学说，跟民众教养的任何程度都合得来；而民众教养也会随着自身的变化逐渐修改这些学说，不过改的多是外在的部分，多是感性想象所描绘的那一面。

en: These doctrines, if they are doctrines grounded on general human reason, can, in that case, by their very constitution have no other purpose than to work only on the spirit of the people at large, partly through themselves, partly through the charm of powerfully penetrating ceremonies bound up with them, so that they will neither mix into the exercise of civil justice nor presume to a private censorship; nor will they — since their formulas too, being simple, easily give occasion to dispute about them — and since they demand and fix little that is positive, but the legislation of reason is only formal — so the lust for rule of the priests of such a religion is limited.
zh: 这些学说，如果它们建立在普遍的人类理性上，那么按其性质就只能有一个目的：一部分靠它们自身，一部分靠与它们相联的、极能打动人心的仪式的魔力，只在大的方面对民族的精神起作用；因此它们既不会插手民事司法的执行，也不会擅自搞什么私下的裁断；而且，由于它们的条文也简单，容易给人机会去就它们本身争论——又由于它们要求的、确定下来的肯定内容很少，而理性的立法只是形式上的——所以这样一种宗教的教士的专权是受到限制的。

en: Every religion that is to be a folk religion must necessarily be so constituted that it occupies heart and imagination.

Even the purest religion of reason becomes embodied in the souls of men, and still more of the people, and it would surely be good, in order to prevent adventurous excesses of the imagination, to connect myths with religion itself from the start, so as at least to show the imagination a beautiful path which it can then strew with flowers. — The doctrines of the Christian religion are for the most part tied to history or presented through it, and the scene is on earth, even if not mere men acted in it; here, then, a goal easy to recognise is set before the imagination, but still a great many places remain where a free room is open to it and it, when coloured with black gall, can paint itself a terrible world, while on the other hand it easily falls into the childish, since what is lovely, the beautiful colours taken from sensuousness, are properly excluded by the spirit of our religion — and we are altogether too much men of reason and of the word to love beautiful images.

As for the ceremonies, on the one hand no folk religion is conceivable without them, but on the other hand there is probably nothing harder than to prevent them from being taken by the mob for the essence of religion itself.
zh: 任何一种要成为民间宗教的宗教，都必然要这样：它能占住人心和想象力。

就连最纯粹的理性宗教，也要在人的灵魂里、在民众的灵魂里更加如此地取得形体；而为了防备想象力胡闯乱跑，一开始就把神话跟宗教本身结合起来，恐怕是好的，这样至少能给想象力指一条美的路，让它随后可以在上面撒满花朵。——基督教宗教的学说大部分是附在历史上、或是通过历史来表述的，舞台就在地上，尽管在其中行动的并不只是人；这样，就给想象力表象出一个容易认出的目标，但仍然留下许多地方，让它有自由活动的余地：它若被黑色的胆汁染过，就能给自己画出一个可怕的世界；可另一方面，它又很容易变得孩子气，因为真正可爱的、那些从感性里取来的美丽色彩，被我们宗教的精神排除掉了——而且我们本来就太是讲理性、讲字句的人，爱不来美的图像。
至于仪式，一方面，没有仪式的民间宗教是不可想象的；另一方面，恐怕再没有比这更难的事：不让群氓把仪式当成宗教本身的本质。

en: Religion consists of three things: a) concepts, b) essential usages, c) ceremonies.

If we regard baptism and the Lord's Supper as rites to which certain extraordinary benefits and graces are bound, which are laid upon us as duties in themselves, whose exercise makes us Christians more perfect, more moral, then they belong to the second class.
But if we regard them merely as means whose purpose and effect is only the awakening of pious feelings, then they belong to the third class.
zh: 宗教由三样东西构成：a）概念，b）本质性的习俗，c）仪式。
如果我们把洗礼和圣餐看作这样一种礼仪：某些特别的恩惠和恩典系于其上，而这些恩惠是作为义务本身加在我们身上的，履行它们会使我们基督徒更完满、更有道德，那么它们就属于第二类。
但如果我们只把它们看作手段，其目的和效果仅仅是唤起虔诚的感受，那它们就归入第三类。

en: Sacrifices also belong here, but can only improperly be called ceremonies, because in the religion with which they are connected they are essential, belong to the building itself, whereas ceremonies are only the ornaments, the forms of this building.
zh: 献祭也属于这一类，但只能不严格地叫作仪式，因为它们在与之相联的那种宗教里是本质性的，属于建筑物本身；而仪式只是这座建筑的装饰、是它的形式。

en: Sacrifices too can be considered from two sides.
zh: 献祭也可以从两个方面来看。

en: a) In part they were offered at the altars of the gods as expiatory sacrifices, as indulgence, as transformation of the feared physical or moral punishment into a fine, as ingratiation into the lost grace of the overlord, the dispenser of rewards and punishments — whereby, in judgements of the worthlessness of such a custom, its irrationality and the falsification of the concept of morality are rightly censured, but at the same time it must be borne in mind that the idea of sacrifice has nowhere (except perhaps in the Christian church) in fact existed so utterly crudely12), and then also that the value of the feelings that were at work in it, even if they were not unmixed — holy awe before the holy being, the humiliating prostration, contrition of heart before it, the confidence that the burdened soul sighing for rest drove to this anchor — must not be entirely misjudged.

A pilgrim pressed by the burden of his sins, who leaves comfort, wife and child, his native soil, to wander the world barefoot and in a hair shirt, who seeks pathless regions to make his feet hurt, and wets the holy places with his tears, seeks rest for his struggling, torn spirit, finds relief in every shed tear, in every penance, in every self-sacrifice, and at the thought, here Christ walked, here he was crucified for me, is cheered and receives again some strength, again some confidence in himself — should such a pilgrim with the simplicity of his heart, for one to whom such a mood is no longer possible because of other concepts of his time, should he then awaken in us the Pharisee feeling: I am cleverer than such people? or should these holy feelings become an object of mockery for us?
Such penances too are of the kind of sacrifices I spoke of here, which are offered from the same spirit as those penances are performed.
zh: a）一部分献祭是献在神的祭坛上的，作为赎罪祭、作为赦免、作为把所惧怕的肉体或道德上的惩罚换成一笔罚金、作为讨好那失去的恩宠——那恩宠属于赏罚的主宰；——在评判这样一种习俗毫无价值时，人们固然有理由指责它不合理性、指责它败坏了道德的概念，但同时也必须想到：献祭这一观念实际上在任何地方都没有（也许除了基督教会）以如此粗陋的样子存在过12）；而且，其中起作用的那些感受——对神圣存在的神圣敬畏、在它面前屈辱地俯伏、心里痛悔、以及那种信赖：负担沉重、叹息着求安宁的灵魂被赶到这个锚地来——即使并不纯粹，其价值也不该完全被看错。

一个朝圣者，被自己的罪压得沉重，离开舒适、离开妻子儿女、离开故土，赤着脚、穿着粗毛衣服去走遍世界，专找没路的地方走，好让自己的脚吃苦，用自己的眼泪打湿那些圣地，为自己那挣扎着、撕扯着的精神寻求安宁，在每一滴流下的眼泪里、在每一次忏悔里、在每一次自我牺牲里得到缓解，一想到这里是基督走过的地方、这里是他为我被钉上十字架的地方，就又振作起来，重新得到一点力量、一点对自己的信心——这样一个朝圣者，带着他心里的单纯，对于一个由于自己时代另有一套概念而再也不可能有这种心境的人来说，难道他该在我们心里唤起那种法利赛人的感觉——我比这种人聪明？还是说，这些神圣的感受该成为我们嘲笑的对象？
这类忏悔苦行也属于我在这里说到的那种献祭，它们与那些苦行是出自同样的精神而做出来的。

en: b) Another, milder shape of sacrifice, sprung from a gentler clime, is probably the more original and more universal one, which was founded on gratitude and benevolence, where the feeling of a being that is more exalted than man, the consciousness that one has to thank it for everything and that it does not disdain what one offers it in innocence, and the sentiment, at the beginning of every undertaking to entreat it first for assistance, at every joy, at every attained happiness to think first of it, of Nemesis before every enjoyment bestowed, to bring it the first-fruits, the flower of every good — [this sentiment] invites this being and hopes that it will dwell kindly around man; — the sentiment that brought such a sacrifice was far from the thought of sins and [from the thought] of having made some atonement for their deserved punishments, or his conscience did not on that account persuade him that Nemesis was thereby satisfied and had on that account given up its claims upon him and its laws in the restoration of the moral equilibrium.
zh: b）献祭还有另一种更温和的形态，它长在更柔和的天底下，大概也是更原本、更普遍的；它建立在感恩和善意上面：在这里，人面对一个比人更高的存在，心里有一种感觉，也意识到自己一切都得感谢它，而它并不嫌弃人在无辜中献给它的东西；同时怀着这样的心意：每开始做一件事，都先求它相助，每逢快乐、每得到一份幸福，都先想到它，每有一份享用，都先想到复仇女神；把初熟的果子、每样好东西的花朵献给它，请这个存在前来，希望它友善地待在人的周围；——献上这种祭的那种心意，离罪的想法很远，也离〔借此为这些罪应得的惩罚赎去了一点〕的想法很远；或者说，他的良心并不因此就劝他说：复仇女神已经由此满足，因此放弃了对他的要求，也放弃了它在重建道德平衡时的法则。

en: Such essential customs of a religion must properly be no more closely connected with it than with the spirit of the people, and must properly have sprouted out of this spirit — otherwise their practice is without life, cold, powerless, the feelings one has in them are contrived, pumped up; or they are customs that are not essential to folk religion but can be so for private religion — thus the Lord's Supper in the shape it now has among Christians, although its proper destination was a meal for enjoyment in company.
zh: 宗教的这些本质性的习俗，其实跟宗教本身的联系，并不比跟民族精神的联系更近，而且本该是从民族精神里长出来的——否则它们的实行就没有生命，冷淡、没有力气，人们在其中有的感受是做作的、硬挤出来的；或者它们是一些对民间宗教并非本质的习俗，但对私人宗教却可以是本质的——比如圣餐，按它如今在基督徒中间的样子，尽管它本来的规定其实是大家一起享用的一顿饭。

en: The necessary properties of the ceremonies of a folk religion are:
zh: 民间宗教的仪式必须具备的性质是：

en: a) and above all, that they can as little as possible become an occasion for fetish service, that they are [not so] constituted that only the work, the mechanism, remains and the spirit flies away.

Their purpose must be solely to heighten devotion, the holy feelings — and as such a pure means, which is least capable of misuse and brings about this effect, perhaps only sacred music and the singing of a whole people remains, perhaps also folk festivals, into which religion must mingle.
zh: a）尤其是：它们要尽可能不成为拜物崇拜的由头，它们的性质〔不能〕是只剩下那套做法、那套机械动作，而精神却飞走了。
它们的目的只能是提高虔诚、提高那些神圣的感受；——而作为一种纯粹的手段，最不容易被滥用、又能产生这种效果，大概只剩下了神圣的音乐和一整个民族的歌唱，也许还有民间节庆，宗教必须掺和到里面去。

en: As soon as there is a dividing wall between life and doctrine, or even only a separation and a wide distance of the two from each other, the suspicion arises that the form of the religion has a fault — either that it busies itself too much with word-mongering, or that it makes too great, sanctimonious demands on men, is contrary to their natural needs, to the drives of a well-ordered sensuousness — τῆς σωφροσύνης — or that both are the case at once.

If men's joys, the cheerfulness of men, have to be ashamed before religion, if from a public festival the one who made merry must sneak into the temple, then the form of the religion has too gloomy an outside for it to be allowed to promise itself that people would give up the joys of life for its demands.
zh: 一旦生活与教义之间隔着一堵墙，或者两者只是彼此分开、相距很远，人就会怀疑宗教的形式有毛病——要么是它太多地纠缠于字眼的买卖，要么是对人提出太大的、装虔诚的要求，跟人的自然需要、跟一种井然有序的感性的冲动——τῆς σωφροσύνης——相违背，要么是两者同时如此。
如果人的欢乐、人的快活要在宗教面前感到羞愧，如果在公共节庆上，那个寻欢作乐的人必须溜进神庙里去，那么宗教的形式就有一副太阴沉的外表，它不能指望人们会为了它的要求而舍弃生活的欢乐。

en: It must dwell kindly around all the feelings of life, must not want to push itself in, but be welcome everywhere.

If religion is to be able to work on the people, it must accompany them kindly everywhere, stand at their side in their business and the more serious affairs of life as well as in their festivals and joys — but not in such a way that it seemed to push itself forward or became a burdensome tutor, but so that it is the leader, the encourager.
The folk festivals of the Greeks were surely all religious festivals, in honour of a god or of a man well deserving of their state and therefore deified.
Everything, even the excesses of the Bacchants, was consecrated to a god; even their public plays had a religious origin, which in their further development they never disowned.
Thus Agathon did not forget the gods when he carried off the prize with a tragedy — the next day he gave the gods a festival.
Sympos[ion] p. 168 [Steph.
zh: 它必须友善地待在生活的所有感受周围，不想硬挤进来，而是处处受到欢迎。
宗教若要能对民众起作用，就必须友善地处处陪着他们，在他们的营生和生活中较严肃的事情上，如同在他们的节庆和欢乐中一样，站在他们身旁；——但不是显得硬要挤进来，或者变成一个累人的家庭教师，而是要做领头的人、鼓劲的人。
希腊人的民间节庆大概全都是宗教节庆，是为了敬奉一位神，或者敬奉一个对国家有功、因此被奉为神的人。
一切，连酒神女信徒们的放纵，都是献给神的；就连他们的公共戏剧也有宗教的来源，在后来进一步发展中也从不否认这一点。
阿伽通凭一部悲剧得了奖，也没有忘记神们；——第二天他就为神们办了一场庆典。
《会饮》第168页〔斯特凡努斯

en: Folk religion, which produces and nourishes great sentiments, goes hand in hand with freedom.
zh: 民间宗教产生并滋养伟大的信念，它跟自由是手挽手同行的。

en: Our religion wants to educate men into citizens of heaven, whose gaze is always directed upwards, and in doing so human feelings become foreign to them.

At our greatest public festival one approaches the enjoyment of the holy gift in the colour of mourning, with downcast gaze — at the festival that should be the festival of universal brotherhood, many a one fears being infected from the brotherly cup by a man with a venereal disease who partook of it before him, and so that his mind may certainly not be kept attentive, not in holy feelings, one must during the act reach the offering out of one's pocket and lay it on the plate — while the Greeks, with the friendly gifts of nature, crowned with flowers, clothed in the colours of joys, spreading gladness on their open faces that invited friendship and love, approached the altars of their good gods.
zh: 我们的宗教要把人教育成天国的公民，让他们的目光永远朝上；这样一来，人的情感对他们就变得陌生了。

在我们最盛大的公共节庆上，人们是带着哀悼的颜色、低垂着目光去领受那份神圣礼物的；——在这个本该是普遍兄弟情谊的节庆上，有人还怕从那只兄弟的杯子里，被前一个喝过杯的、患花柳病的人传染；而且为了务使他的心不专注、不保持在神圣的感受里，他在仪式进行时还得从口袋里掏出献品，放到盘子上；——而希腊人呢，带着自然给的好意礼物，头上戴着花环，身上穿着欢乐的颜色，在敞开的、邀请人做朋友和相爱的脸上流露着快乐，走向他们那些善良的神的祭坛。

en: The spirit of a people, its history, its religion, the degree of its political freedom can be considered neither with respect to their influence on one another nor with respect to their constitution in separation; they are woven together into one bond — as of three colleagues in office none can do anything without the others, but each also takes something from the others.

To form the morality of individual men is the business of a private religion, of parents, of one's own effort and of circumstances; to form the spirit of a people is partly also the business of folk religion, partly of political conditions.14)
zh: 民族精神、历史、宗教、一个民族政治自由的程度，既不能就它们彼此的影响分开来看，也不能就它们各自的样子分开来看；它们被编织在一条带子里——就像三个同事，谁离了别人也做不成事，但每个人也从别人那里得到点什么。
培养单个人的道德，是私人宗教的事，是父母的事，是自己的努力和环境的事；培养民族精神，一部分也是民间宗教的事，一部分是政治状况的事。14)

en: Ah, from the far-off days of the past there shines towards the soul that has feeling for human beauty, for greatness in great things, an image — the image of a genius of peoples, of a son of fortune, of freedom, of a pupil of beautiful imagination.

Him too the brazen bond of needs bound to mother earth, but through his feeling, through his imagination he has so worked it, refined it, beautified it, with the help of the Graces wound it about with roses, that in these fetters he pleases himself as in his own work, as in a part of himself.

His servants were joy, cheerfulness, grace; his soul [was] filled with the consciousness of its strength and its freedom; his more serious playfellows, friendship and love, [were] not the forest faun, but the finely feeling, soulful Amor adorned with all the charms of the heart and of lovely dreams.
zh: 啊，从过去那些遥远的日子里，有一幅图像向那种对人间的美、对大的东西中的伟大还有感觉的心灵照过来——那是一个民族天才的图像，一个幸运之子、自由之子的图像，一个由美的想象力带大的孩子的图像。
需要的青铜锁链也把他拴在大地母亲身上，但他用自己的感受、用自己的想象力把它加工、琢磨、美化，靠着美惠女神们的手给它缠上玫瑰，以至于他在这副锁链里，就像在自己的作品里、在自己的一部分里一样，感到惬意。
他的仆人是快乐、快活和优美；他的心灵〔是〕充满对自己力量和自由的意识的；他那些较严肃的玩伴，友谊和爱，〔不是〕林中的法乌诺斯，而是感受细腻、有灵魂、被心和可爱梦境的一切魅力装扮起来的阿莫尔。

en: From his father, a favourite of fortune and a son of strength, he received as inheritance confidence in his fortune and pride in his deeds.

His indulgent mother, no scolding, hard woman, left her son to the upbringing of nature, did not force his tender limbs into constricting swaddling-clothes, and as a good mother she followed the moods, the whims of her darling rather than restraining them.

In harmony with these, the nurse, [in dealing with] him, the child of nature, was not to want to bring him up and form him into a youth with fear of the rod or of a spectre of darkness, not with the sour-sweet sugar-bread of mysticism that slackens the stomach, nor on the leading-string of words that would have kept him in eternal immaturity, but she gave him to drink of the purer, healthy milk of pure feelings — led by the hand of beautiful, free imagination, she adorned with her flowers the impenetrable veil that withdraws the Godhead from our gaze, peopled and conjured behind it living images, onto which he transferred the great ideas of his own heart with the whole fullness of high and beautiful feelings. — As the nurse among the Greeks was a friend of the house and remained the friend of her pupil her whole life long, so she remained always his friend, to whom he brings undefiled his free thanks, free love, [she] shares as a sociable friend his joys, his games, and [he] is not disturbed by her in his joys, she maintains her dignity thereby, and his own conscience punishes any neglect of it; she keeps her dominion forever, for it is built on love, on gratitude, on the noblest feelings of her pupil — she flattered her own adornment, obeyed the mood of his imagination, but she taught him to honour iron necessity, she taught him to follow this unchangeable fate without murmuring.
zh: 他从父亲那里得到一份遗产——父亲是命运的宠儿、力量的儿子——那就是对自己运气的信心和对自己作为的骄傲。
他宽容的母亲不是那种爱骂人、硬心肠的女人，她把儿子交给自然去教育，不用捆得紧紧的襁褓去束缚他柔嫩的肢体；作为一个好母亲，她更多是顺着自己宝贝的心情和念头，而不是去限制它们。

跟这些相配，乳母对待他这个自然的孩子，就不该想用对棍子的恐惧、用黑暗中的鬼怪来把他带大、把他教养成人，也不该用神秘主义那种叫人胃里发软的又酸又甜的糖面包，更不该用言语的牵引带——那会让他永远处于未成年状态；她给他喝的是纯净感受的更清亮、更健康的奶——她牵着美的、自由的想象力的手，用她的花装扮那道把神从我们眼前遮住的、穿不透的面纱，还在面纱后面造出、变出活的图像，他把自己心里的伟大观念，连同崇高而美好的感受的全部丰富，都移到了这些图像上。——就像希腊人家里乳母是家中之友，一辈子都是学生的朋友一样，她也始终是他的朋友：他向她献上未被败坏的、自由的感谢和自由的爱，她作为能交往的朋友分享他的快乐、他的游戏，他在快乐中也不受她打扰，她在这当中保持着自己的尊严，而他自己良心里也会责备对她的任何疏忽；她的统治永远不倒，因为它建立在爱、建立在感恩、建立在她的学生最高贵的情感上面——她奉承自己的妆饰，听从他想入非非的兴致，但她教他尊敬铁的必然性，教他毫无怨言地跟随这不可更改的命运。

en: We know this genius only from hearsay, only a few traits of him, in surviving copies of his shape, are we granted to contemplate with love and admiration, which awaken only a painful longing for the original.

He is the beautiful youth whom we love also in his levity, with the whole retinue of the Graces, with them the balsamic breath of nature, the soul which, breathed into him by them, he sucked from every flower, - he has fled from the earth.15)
zh: 这个天才我们只是听说的，只有他的几笔特征，留在他形象的摹本里，我们才有幸带着爱与赞叹去端详，而这只会唤起对原本的一种痛苦渴慕。
他就是那个漂亮的少年，我们连他的轻浮也一并喜爱，他身边跟着整整一队美惠女神，随她们而来的还有大自然那沁人的气息，还有那灵魂——她们把它吹进他身里，他便从每一朵花中把它吸了进去——如今他已从大地上飞走了。15）

en: 16) One teaches our children table prayers, morning and evening blessings –
zh: 16）人们教我们的孩子做饭前祷告、早晚祝福——

en: Our tradition - folk songs, etc. It is no Harmodius, no Aristogeiton, whom eternal glory accompanied, since they struck down the tyrant and gave equal rights and laws to their citizens, who lived in the mouth of our people, in its songs.
zh: 我们的传统——民歌等等。并没有一个哈尔摩狄乌斯，没有一个阿里斯托革顿，他们因为打倒了僭主、给自己的公民争得平等的权利和法律，身后跟着永久的荣光，活在人民的嘴里、活在他们自己的歌里。

en: What is the historical knowledge of our people?

[A] peculiar, fatherland-ish tradition is lacking to it, the memory, the imagination is filled with the primeval history of mankind, with the history of a foreign people, with the deeds and misdeeds of their kings, which do not concern us at all - and wit exercises itself as well on their absurdities as the wit of an Aristophanes on his gods.
zh: 我们人民的历史知识是什么呢？
他缺的是一种特有的、本乡本土的传统；记忆和想象力塞满的是人类的远古史，是一个外族的历史，是他们国王的作为和胡作非为——那些跟我们毫不相干——于是才智就在他们的可笑之处上练手，正如阿里斯托芬的才智在自己的诸神身上练手。

en: Not to be denied are the perverse and immoral notions of the Jews about wrath, partiality, hatred of other peoples, the intolerance of their Jehovah, - notions which unfortunately have passed over into the practice and theory of the Christian religion and have caused too much damage for one not to wish that they had had their origin in a more friend-of-man religion or that it had taken over less of them.

And we have to thank not their priests, but philosophy, by which [sc. the priests] it was hated on that account, and the milder light of our times, that their gloomy quarrelsomeness, their intolerance and their self-conceit have diminished.

While the champions of orthodoxy defended it against the giants by whom it was attacked, they gradually took over notions of theirs themselves, and the only way out, to save the main fortress, was to give up the untenable outworks and, in order after all to give up nothing of the glory, to say afterwards that one had not intended to defend these, like the general who in the evening still held the field of battle and had the blowing postillions proclaim his victory in the capital, who indeed thereby impressed the mob, which believes it and strikes up a Te Deum, yet often is not the actual victor, but betrays himself through the following evacuation of the region; so too theology did not have the word, but the difference of its compendia after 10-20 years.
zh: 不可否认的是犹太人对愤怒、偏袒、对其他民族的仇恨、对他们的耶和华的不宽容所抱的那些颠倒的、不道德的概念——可惜这些概念传进了基督教宗教的实践和理论，造成的危害太大，人不能不希望它们当初是出自一种更爱人类的宗教，或者这种宗教少接受它们一些。
而它们的阴沉的争闹、它们的不宽容和它们的自负之所以减少，我们要感谢的不是它们的教士，而是哲学——教士正因此才恨哲学——以及我们这个时代更温和的光。

正统的卫士们在它遭到巨人攻击时替它辩护，同时自己也渐渐接受了那些巨人的一些概念；而要保住主堡垒，唯一的出路就是放弃那些守不住的外围工事，并且为了到头来一点也不丢掉荣誉，事后说一句：这些工事我本来就没打算守——就像那位将军，傍晚还占着战场，让吹号的车夫在首都宣布他的胜利，这一手固然镇住了群氓，群氓相信了，还唱起《赞美颂》，可他常常并不是真正的胜利者，随后一撤离那片地方就露了馅；神学也是这样，说话算数的不是它，而是它那些教科书十年二十年前后的差别。

en: But if you would be perfect, sell what you have and give your goods to the poor, said Christ to the young man.

This image of perfection that Christ sets up carries in itself the proof of how much Christ in his teaching had before his eyes only the formation and perfection of the single human being and how little it can be extended to a society on the large scale.
zh: 你若愿意作完全人，就去变卖你所有的，把家产分给穷人，基督对那少年说。
基督摆出的这个完善的图像本身就带着证明：基督在教导时眼里只有单个人的教养和完善，这一点多么不可能推广到一个大范围的社会上去。

en: The opponents of Christianity have set out the corruptness of the Christians, especially of the clergy, very bitingly and in part bitterly, as a proof against its truth and beneficence; its defenders declare this to be the weakest, though brilliant, attack, - yet if it is so effective, its main essence should still not be misrecognisable; moral improvement [is found] least of all in those whose business it is to reflect on it always from youth on.

Their excuse is always that the Christian religion has been misrecognised, yet they had the Bible as well as we; they give to understand that only their compendium was lacking, if that had been out, everything would have gone differently.

Has it opposed despotism? - how long is it, then, that it has opposed the slave trade? its priests go along with the ships to Guinea, - or the trade in human beings? one sends field chaplains along, - the wars? despotism of every kind?
The arts, the enlightenment have improved our morals, and afterwards one says that the Christian religion did this, that without it philosophy would not have found its principles.
zh: 基督教的对手们把基督徒的败坏、尤其是教士阶层的败坏，当作反对它的真理性和造福作用的证据，讲得十分尖刻，有些地方还很苦涩；它的辩护者说这是最弱的一击，虽然很耀眼——可它既然这样起作用，那它的主要本质总不该认不出来吧；道德的改善，恰恰最少见于那些从少年起就以反复琢磨道德为业的人身上。
他们的辩解永远是：基督教宗教被人误解了。可他们手里的圣经跟我们的一样好啊；他们的意思是，缺的只是他们那本教科书，要是那本书早出来，一切就都另一个样子了。
它抵抗过专制吗？——它抵抗奴隶买卖才有多久呢？他们的教士跟着船去几内亚——那人口买卖呢？人们还派随军牧师跟着——那战争呢？那各种样式的专制呢？
艺术和启蒙改善了我们的道德，事后人们却说这是基督教宗教做的，没有它哲学就找不到自己的原理。

en: If reason sets up the building of concepts that it has drawn from the spirit of man and the experience of centuries, with self-satisfaction and joy in its work, and gives itself airs towards those who presume to have the privilege of these truths and shows itself self-sufficient, that it can do without their source, then that pretence of theirs, as if they had after all supplied the building material and had already long before those discoveries known just as much, indeed more, and still know it now, is just as vain as if a country squire had boasted against Newton that he had already in his fifth year seen apples fall from the trees and had already known then that the sun does not fall onto the earth.
Where has one ever seen a change in religious concepts, by which a happy change in the course of scientific culture was brought about, precede such a change?

Has not rather the widening of the sciences, the spirit of examination in them, always first drawn after it an enlightenment of theological concepts, and that with the greatest possible opposition from the guardians of these concepts?
zh: 如果理性把它从人的精神和数百年的经验中汲取来的概念大厦，带着自我满足和对自身作品的喜悦立起来，并且在那些自以为拥有这些真理特权的人面前摆出一副了不起的样子，还表明自己本身就够用、可以不要自己的来源，那么他们那种说法——仿佛建筑材料毕竟还是他们出的，而且早在那些发现之前就已经知道同样多、甚至更多，现在也还知道——就和一个乡下地主向牛顿夸口一样空虚：他五岁上就看见苹果从树上掉下来了，那时候就已经知道太阳不会掉到地上来。
人们何曾见过，在科学教养的进程中出现一个幸运的变化之前，先有宗教概念上的一个变化，而那个变化又是造成前者的原因呢？
难道不是恰恰相反，科学的扩展、科学中的审查精神，总是先带来神学概念的启蒙，而且是在这些概念的守护者尽可能大的反对之下带来的吗？

en: 17) Apart from oral instruction, which always has only a very limited sphere of effect, extends only to those whom nature has first bound to us, the only mode of effect on the large scale [is] through writings; here the teacher places himself on an invisible pulpit before the whole public, and because he is not seen, he has here the heart to set before it the most glaring pictures of its moral corruption, and deals with it so little sparingly as he would otherwise scarcely adopt a tone towards the most despised human being; one has probably hardly ever seen that, if it did not happen by virtue of office, a moralist ever had the heart to hold up - uncalled, merely driven by inner feeling of a vocation, to better human beings - even half of what he says to the face of the whole public, highly honoured according to rank and dignity, before the circle of human beings from which, if his picture is not otherwise mere radotage and his means against it mere theoretical quackery, he had abstracted the traits for it.
As in general the manner of instruction must always orient itself by the genius and the tone with which one can get anywhere with a people, so we find the manner different here too.

Socrates, who lived in a republican state where every citizen spoke freely with the other, but where a fine urbanity in intercourse was the share even of the lowest mob, climbed onto people's roofs in conversation in the most unprejudiced way in the world, and without the didactic tone, without the appearance of wanting to instruct, he began an ordinary conversation and led in the finest way to a doctrine that gave itself of itself and could not seem obtrusive even to a Diotima.

The Jews, by contrast, were already used, from their forefathers on, to being harangued in a rougher way by their national poets, already from their synagogues on their ears were [used] to moral sermons and a direct tone of instruction, from their scribes' and Pharisees' quarrelling to a coarser manner of refuting opponents, and so from one who was not exactly a Pharisee or Sadducee either, an address like "you brood of snakes and vipers" did not sound to them so hard as it would have sounded to Greek ears.
zh: 17）除了口头教导——它的作用范围总是很有限，只涉及那些自然最先与我们连在一起的人——之外，大范围里唯一的作用方式就是靠文字；在这里，教导者站上一个看不见的讲坛，面对整个公众，而且因为他不会被看见，他在这里才有胆量给它摆出它道德败坏的种种最刺眼的图画，跟它打交道时毫不留情，这种语气他平时哪怕对最受鄙视的人也不会用；人们大概很少见过，一个道德家若不是职务上必须如此，会仅仅为内心那种要改善人类的使命感所驱使、不待人请，就有胆量把他当着那个按身份和地位备受尊敬的整个公众的面所说的话——哪怕一半——摆到那圈人面前，而他若不是这样，他的图画就只是胡扯，他对付它的手段就只是理论上的假药，可他的那些笔触毕竟是从这圈人身上取来的。
本来就总的说来，教导的方式必须依从一个民族身上能打动人的那种气质和调子，所以我们在这里也看到方式各不相同。
苏格拉底生活在一个共和制的国家里，那里每个公民都和别人自由交谈，但与人交往中那种细腻的风度，连最下等的群氓也分得一份；他就用世上最不客气的方式在聊天中爬到别人头上去，没有教训人的调子，没有要教导谁的样子，他起头只是一场平常的谈话，然后以最精细的方式引到一条道理上，这条道理是自己冒出来的，连一位狄奥提玛也不会觉得它是在硬塞给人。
犹太人却不同，他们从祖先起就已经习惯被自己的民族诗人用更粗的方式训话，从会堂里起耳朵就已经习惯了道德说教和那种直接的教训口气，从他们的文士和法利赛人的争吵里习惯了更粗鲁的反驳对手的方式，所以从一个人嘴里——哪怕这人并不正好是法利赛人或撒都该人——说出"你们这些蛇类、毒蛇之种"这样的话，听起来并不像在希腊人耳朵里那么刺耳。

en: One should think that a human being could always, even with the best dispositions and the most excellent upbringing, never cease his whole life long to work on his intellectual and moral perfection, and that an unprejudiced man active in this could never easily be finished with himself, or believe himself to be, in the manifold relations into which he is placed partly by chance with other human beings, partly into which his own activity, always still to learn something, brings him, and this all the more in the entangled relations of our civil life, where often even the most decided uprightness will find itself in an ambiguous collision of duties, e.g. frequently between equity and compassion in the individual case and general principles of justice or at least of time-honoured rights - and where prudence all the more must be careful out of duty when it does not attend to its own affairs, but helps to promote a branch of well-being of a larger multitude of human beings, in the greater or in the smaller.

Hence also many a conscientious Nathanael has already preferred to place himself wholly out of these relations, in order not to have to do violence to his heart or in order to spare himself the embarrassments; for the more manifold the relations, the more manifold the duties, and so the simpler those, the simpler also these, and it usually costs more self-overcoming to step out than not to enter at all - just as it is easier to do without other needs than to renounce them voluntarily.

A Diogenes, then, whose temperament can put up with a handful of water and a bad piece of bread and whose ambition is satisfied [is] not by a purple robe but by a torn cloak, who therefore neither as friend, nor as father, nor through his acquisition has any further great duties towards others than not to hit them and - to which he can hardly be tempted - not to steal, he has made it easy for himself to be a perfect moral man, and has even acquired a kind of right to be called a great man, he has time and while enough now to work on others too.
zh: 人总该可以，哪怕天赋最好、受教育最好，一辈子都不停止在自己的理智和道德的完善上下功夫；一个毫无成见、又在这上面用功的人，处在种种关系里——有些是他和别人被偶然摆进去的，有些是他自己的活动把他带进去的，因为总还有东西要学——总不该轻易就和自己了结，或者以为自己已经了结了；在我们市民生活的纠缠关系里就更是如此，那里往往连最坚定的正直也会落到义务的含混冲突里，比如常在个别情形下的公平和同情，与正义的普遍原理、或者至少是久已生效的权利之间——那里精明若是办的不是自己的事，而是帮着在较大或较小的范围里促进一大群人的某一份福祉，就更加必须出于义务而谨慎。
所以也已经有不少良心上过不去的拿但业，宁可干脆把自己从这些关系里抽出来，免得对自己的心用强，或者免得给自己招来这些为难；因为关系越多样，义务就越多样，那些关系越简单，这些义务也越简单；而要退出来，通常比压根不进去更费力——就像免去别的需要比自愿放弃它们更容易一样。
所以一个第欧根尼，他的性情拿一把水、一块坏面包就能将就，他的虚荣心不是靠一件紫袍、而是靠一件破斗篷就得到满足，他因此既不是作为朋友、也不是作为父亲、也不是靠自己的营生，而对别人再没有更多的大义务，只是不去打人，以及不去偷东西——这一点他不容易受到诱惑——他给自己把做一个完善的道德人这件事弄得很轻松，甚至还挣得了一种被称为大人的资格；他有的是时间和工夫，现在也可以在别人身上用功了。

en: Among the Romans no Christ rose up, no Socrates; no Roman in the times of their strength, when only one virtue counted, could be at a loss to know what he had to do — there were only Romans in Rome, no human beings; in Greece, on the other hand, the studia humanitatis were prized, human feelings, human inclinations and arts, and there were several kinds of by-paths away from nature, to which a Socrates or some other wise man could think of leading [men] back — deviation from the Roman nature was a crime against the state.

Where men have laid down some line of perfection and tied virtue to something objective, in whose service the passions themselves can become virtues, there it is easier to judge what approaches it or deviates from it than it is where a higher interest is present and, in the throng of manifold colliding duties — or in the strengthening of human inclinations and duties — virtue and the limit up to which nature ought to subject itself to reason are infinitely harder to distinguish.
zh: 在罗马人中间，没有站出来过一个基督，也没有站出来过一个苏格拉底；在罗马人强盛的年代，那时只算得上一种美德，没有一个罗马人会为不知道自己该做什么而为难——在罗马只有罗马人，没有人；而在希腊，人们看重 studia humanitatis，也就是人的情感、人的偏好和种种技艺，偏离自然的岔路也有好几种，一个苏格拉底或别的什么智者可以想到把人领回自然去——偏离罗马的本性却是国家罪。
凡是人们定下了某条完善的界线、把美德系在某种客观的东西上，以至于连各种激情都可以在替它效劳时变成美德，那里就比较容易判断什么在向它靠近、什么在偏离它；而在有一种更高的关切在起作用的地方，在各种互相冲突的义务挤作一团的时候——或者在人的偏好和义务变得强劲的时候——美德，以及自然应当服从理性到哪一步这条界线，却要难分辨得多。

en: Christ had twelve apostles, the number twelve was a fixed, abiding number — he had several disciples, but the apostles were those who enjoyed his intimate company, who had cast off all other relations and enjoyed only his company, his instruction, who strove to become as like him as possible in everything — sought to take possession of his spirit through the length of time, of the instruction and of his living example; and how narrowly Jewish, how entirely earthly their expectations, hopes, ideas were at first, and how slowly they could raise and widen their gaze and their heart from a Jewish Messiah and founder of a kingdom in which general and court-marshal posts were to be handed out, and from the self-interest that thinks first of itself, to the mere ambition of becoming a fellow citizen of the kingdom of God!

It was not enough for Christ to have disciples like Nathanael, Joseph of Arimathea, Nicodemus and the like, i.e. to have had correspondences of thought with men of spirit and of an excellent heart, to have perhaps cast a few new ideas, a few sparks into their soul, which, if the stuff they fall on is not good, [does not] itself contain fuel, are lost in any case — such men, partly happy and content in the evening in the bosom of their family and usefully active in their sphere, partly acquainted with the world and its prejudices, and therefore tolerant towards them, though strict towards themselves, would not have been receptive to the demand to become a kind of adventurer.

Christ says, the kingdom of God does not show itself with outward gestures; so it seems his disciples misunderstood him in the command, Go ye into all the world etc. and baptize them, insofar as they held this baptism, an outward sign, to be universally necessary, which is all the more harmful since distinction by outward signs brings sectarianism, separation from others in its train — [as] in general the distinction through the moral is weakened by the fact that yet another distinction is conceded alongside it, and as it were already loses from its illumination.

Christ says: whoever believes — but it does not say precisely: whoever believes in me — whether or not that is to be understood by it, the apostles once took it that way, and the shibboleth of their friends, of the citizens of their kingdom of God, was not: virtue, uprightness, but: Christ, baptism, etc. — Had their Christ not been such a good man — see Nathan [II, 1].
zh: 基督有十二个使徒，十二这个数目是一个固定的、持存的数目——他有好几个门徒，但使徒是那些享受他亲密交往的人，他们抛开了其他一切关系，只享受他的交往、他的教导，尽力在一切事上变得尽可能像他——想靠时间的漫长、靠教导和他的活的榜样，把他的精神据为己有；而他们起初的期待、希望、观念是多么狭隘地犹太式、多么完全地尘世式，他们又是多么缓慢地才能把自己的眼光和心，从一个犹太的弥赛亚、一个将要有大将和宫廷元帅职位可以封授的国度的创立者，从那种首先想到自己的自私自利，抬高、拓宽到仅仅去追求成为上帝之国的一个同胞！

基督并不满足于有拿但业、亚利马太的约瑟、尼哥底母之类的门徒，也就是说，并不满足于跟有精神、有卓越心肠的人有思想上的来往，往他们的灵魂里投进几个新观念、几点火星——这些火星，如果落下去的地方材料不好、本身不含燃料，反正也是白丢——这样的人，有的晚上在家人怀里过得幸福满足，在自己的活动范围里做着有益的事，有的熟悉世界和它的种种偏见，因此对世界宽容，对自己却严格，他们对于“去当一种冒险家”这样的要求是不会接受的。
基督说，上帝之国不是靠外在的姿势显出来的；这样看来，他的门徒在“你们要去，传遍万民……给他们施洗”这道命令上，多少是误解了他：他们竟把洗礼这个外在的记号看作普遍必要的；这格外有害，因为靠外在记号来区分，会带来宗派作风，带来跟别人的疏远——一般说来，靠道德而有的区分，一旦还容许另一种区分并存，就被削弱了，仿佛连自己的光照也失去了。
基督说：凡信的人——但并没有明说：凡信我的人——不管这里该不该这样理解，使徒们反正当初就是这么理解的，而他们那些朋友、他们上帝之国的公民的暗语，不是美德、正直，而是：基督、洗礼等等——要不是他们那位基督是这么好一个人——见《纳坦》[II, 1]。

en: Socrates had disciples of every kind; or rather he had none — he was only a teacher and master, as every man distinguished by his example of uprightness and by excellent reason is for everyone.

Even if one did not hear him preach from a lectern or down from a mountain — how should it ever have occurred to a Socrates in Greece to preach? He set out to instruct men, to enlighten them about what ought to awaken their highest interest and to animate them for it; he did not let himself be paid for his wisdom; for its sake he did not drive his unkind wife out of the house, as if he wanted to have nothing to do with her, but remained without ill will, with no harm to his wisdom, in his relations as a man, as a father.
zh: 苏格拉底有各式各样的学生；或者不如说他没有学生——他只是一个教师和师傅，就像每一个以正直的榜样和出众的理性而显得杰出的人，对任何人来说都是这样。
就算人们不曾听见他站在讲台上或从山上下来布道——在希腊，一个苏格拉底怎么想得到去布道呢？他所做的就是教导人，把人身上应当唤起最高关切的东西讲明白，并为他们把它鼓动起来；他不靠自己的智慧挣钱；他也不为了智慧就把那个不温柔的妻子赶出家门，好像要跟她一刀两断，而是毫无反感地、在不损害自己智慧的情况下，留在做男人、做父亲的种种关系里。

en: The number of his closer friends was indeterminate; the 13th, 14th, etc. was as welcome to him as the preceding ones, if only he was their equal in spirit and heart.

They were his friends, his disciples, yet in such a way that each remained for himself what he was, that Socrates did not live in them, was not the head from which they as members received the sap of life.

He had no mould into which he wanted to cast his characters, no rules according to which he wanted to even out their differences — for that only small spirits would have been at his disposal, whom he did indeed take up, but who precisely did not become his most intimate friends —; it was not his concern to plane himself a little corps as his bodyguard, in the same uniform, the same drill, the same password, who together would have only one spirit, and who would then have borne his name forever — hence there have indeed been Socratics, but never a guild that could have been told apart, like the masons, by hammer and trowel.

Each of his disciples was a master for himself; many founded schools of their own, several were great generals, statesmen, heroes of every kind — not of one and the same stamp, each in a field of his own, not heroes in martyrdom and suffering, but in action and in life.

Besides, the fisherman remained whoever was a fisherman, no one was to leave house and home — he began with each man from his trade and so led him from the hand to the spirit, from a matter in which each man was at home, with which he conversed with him; he developed out of the soul of man the concepts that lay in it and needed nothing further than a midwife: he gave no one occasion to say: How — is this not the son of Sophroniscus?
Where does such wisdom come to him, that he presumes to teach us?

He offended no one by making much of his importance or by mysterious, lofty phrases, which may impress only the ignorant and the credulous — [otherwise] he would have become an object of laughter among the Greeks.
zh: 他较亲近的朋友有多少是不定的；第十三个、第十四个等等，只要在精神和心肠上跟他相当，就同前面那些一样受欢迎。
他们是他的朋友、他的学生，但每个人仍旧是他自己本来的样子，苏格拉底并不活在他们里面，并不是那个头，而他们作为肢体从他那里获得生命的汁液。
他没有一个模子，想把自己的性格都浇进去；也没有一些规则，想借它们把各人的差异抹平——真要用这些，他手里也只有些小精神可用，他固然也照管过这些人，但他们恰恰没有成为他最亲近的朋友——他并不想给自己刨出一小支卫队，穿一样的制服、做一样的操练、喊一样的口令，合起来只有一种精神，然后永远打着他苏格拉底的名号——所以苏格拉底派的人是有的，却从来没有什么行会，能像泥瓦匠那样凭锤子和抹刀就认得出来。
他的每一个学生自己就是一个师傅；许多人创立了自己的学派，还有不少人成了大将军、政治家、各式各样的英雄——不是同一个模子里出来的，各人在各自的领域里，不是在殉道和受苦中做英雄，而是在行动中、在生活中做英雄。
此外，渔夫仍旧是渔夫，谁也不必离开家业——他跟每个人都是从他的行当开始，就这样把人从手头的事引到精神，从每个人熟悉的一件事、一件他跟他聊起的事引过去；他从人的灵魂里把那些已经躺在里面的概念接生出来，它们需要的不过是一个接生婆：他没有让任何人有机会说：怎么——这不就是索夫罗尼斯科斯的儿子吗？
他这智慧是从哪儿来的，竟敢来教我们？
他不靠摆自己的了不起，也不靠那些神秘的大话去得罪人——那种话只能唬住无知的人和轻信的人——不然他在希腊人中间早就成了笑话。

en: Before his death — he died as a Greek who sacrificed a cock to Aesculapius, not as Maupertuis died in a Capuchin cowl, not as you take communion — before his death, then, he spoke with his disciples about the immortality of the soul, as a Greek speaks, to reason and to imagination — he spoke so vividly, he showed them this hope so near, so convincingly, in his whole being; the premises for this postulate they had gathered in their whole life.

This hope — it contradicts human nature and the capacity of its spirit that so much could be given us that it should become a certainty — he animated up to the point at which the human spirit, forgetting its mortal companion, can lift itself out — that, even if it were to be that a spirit rose from its tomb and brought us news of the avenger18), that he would give us more to hear than the tablets of Moses and the oracles of the prophets which we have in our hearts — that, if this had after all been allowed to be contrary to the laws of human nature, he would not have needed to strengthen it by resurrection — only in poor spirits that do not have living within them the premises of this hope, i.e. the idea of virtue and of the highest good, is the hope of immortality also weak.

He left behind no masonic signs, no command to proclaim his name, no method of climbing onto the roof of the soul and pouring morality into it — the ἀγαθόν is born with us, something that [can]not be preached in.

To bring men to proficiency in the good, he showed no detour (over fragrant flowers that attack the head19) ) that was to pass through him — where he would be the centre, as it were the capital, to which one would have to travel laboriously and from which one would have to transport home the most graciously granted nourishment and put it out at interest — no ordo salutis, where every character, every estate, every age, every temperament would have to go through certain stations of suffering, certain states of soul; rather he knocked straight at the right gate, without mediators, led man only into himself, where he was not to prepare a dwelling for a total stranger, [a] spirit that would arrive from a far country, but was only to make better light and room for his old householder, whom the crowd of fiddlers and pipers would have forced to retreat into an old attic chamber.
zh: 在他死前——他是作为一个向阿斯克勒庇俄斯献上一只公鸡的希腊人死的，不像莫佩尔蒂那样穿着嘉布遣会的僧衣死去，也不像你们领圣餐那样——在他死前，他跟自己的门徒谈论灵魂不死，像一个希腊人那样谈，诉诸理性和想象力——他谈得那么生动，用他的整个为人把这个希望向他们显示得那么近、那么有说服力；这个假设的前提，他们一辈子都在收集。

这个希望——要是它变成确凿无疑的东西，那就跟人的本性、跟人的精神的能力相矛盾——他把它鼓动到这样一个程度：人的精神忘掉自己会死的同伴，能够把自己抬起来——即便真有这样的事，一个精灵从坟墓里爬出来，把那位报应者的消息带给我们18)，即便他能让我们听到比我们心里的摩西石板和先知的神谕更多的东西——即便这当真可以违背人的本性的规律，他也根本不必用复活来加强它——只有在那些贫乏的精神里，它们心里并没有活生生地拥有这个希望的前提，也就是美德和至善的观念，不死的希望才是微弱的。
他没有留下什么共济会的暗号，没有留下宣扬他名字的命令，也没有留下一种方法，好爬到灵魂的屋顶上去、把道德灌进里面——善（ἀγαθόν）是和我们一起生下来的，不是靠布道灌进去的东西。

为了让人们练成行善的熟练，他没有指出一条绕道（穿过芬芳的、冲脑袋的花19)），要人从他那里经过——那样他就是中心，好比是首都，人们得辛辛苦苦地旅行到那里，再把恩赐发放的给养运回家去、拿去生利息——他也没有拿出一套救恩次序，让每一种性格、每一个等级、每一个年龄、每一种气质都得走完某些受苦的站点、某些灵魂状态；他是径直去敲那扇正确的门，不要中介，只把人领进他自己里面；在那里，人不是要给一个完全陌生的客人、一个从远方来的精神准备住处，而只是要给自己原来的房东腾出更好的光和地方——那位房东已经被一大群拉琴吹笛的人逼得退进一间破旧的阁楼小屋里去了。

en: 20) The constitutions, legislations and religions of peoples long continue to bear traces of their original childlike spirit about them, even when this has long since flown away.

For a long time power is still in the hands of a single man, from whom a family let it be exercised with childlike mind as from its father — when the people has long ceased to be a family, and the prince a father.

With regard to constitution and legislation, peoples soon felt, as soon as they expanded a little, that their childlike trust was being abused, and they restricted the evil or good will of their rulers by definite laws.

The childlike spirit in religions has preserved itself longer, and these always bear traces of it about them, when in states no one has long been credited with more good than he is permitted or commanded to do.
zh: 20) 各民族的政体、立法和宗教，长久还带着它们最初那种孩童般精神的痕迹，即使这种精神早已消散。
权力还长久地握在一个人手里，一个家族曾以孩童般的心意让他作为自己的父亲来行使这种权力——而这时人民早已不再是一个家族，君主也早已不再是一位父亲。
在政体和立法方面，各民族一稍有扩张，很快便感到自己那份孩童般的信任被人滥用了，于是用明确的法律把掌权者或坏或好的意愿限制起来。
宗教里那种孩童般的精神保存得更久，宗教身上总是带着它的痕迹，即使在各国的治理中，早已不再指望谁做出比他得到允许或被命令去做的更多的善事。

en: This childlike mind in religion regards God as a mighty lord who besides has inclinations, passions, even moods — God rests —, like the rulers among men, and [who] therefore does not always punish or make happy according to the rule of right, with whom one can therefore ingratiate oneself, against whom one feels more fear, at most awe, than one consecrates love to [him], to whom [one] — as of old and still now to the princes of the Orient — as still now innocence [does] to its patrons or friends — out of the good gifts that nature gives to man — cheerfulness and contentment — offers something, often lays down the fairest, the earliest as a voluntary tribute of trust and joy; — whom the imagination believes nearer here or there, who seems to it to linger more gladly here or there around good, venerable men, around the huts of innocence — of a Baucis —, and who [lets] these places, these men seem holier, more venerable to [it] — σεμνοί, πελώριοι —; — who to the childlike understanding seems to work more immediately in storms, floods, plague, etc., in the surging of the sea, in the threatening of the rocks — the same one or several —; — and upon whom the childlike power of imagination transfers the business and relations of human life.21)
zh: 宗教里这种孩童般的心意，把上帝看成一个有权势的领主，他此外还有偏好、有激情，甚至还有脾气——上帝在休息——就像人间的统治者那样，因此他并不总是按法权的规则来惩罚或赐福；在他面前人可以讨好卖乖，对他更多的是畏惧，顶多是敬畏，而不是把爱奉献给他；人们像古时和现在对东方的君主那样——也像现在无辜的人对自己的恩人、朋友那样——从自然给人的好礼物里，也就是从欢快和满足里，拿出一点来献给他，往往把最美、最早的作为信任和喜悦的自愿贡品存放起来；——想象力觉得他在这里或那里更近，觉得他在这里或那里更愿意待在一些善良可敬的人身边，待在无辜者的茅屋——一位鲍西丝——旁边，并且[让]这些地方、这些人显得更神圣、更可敬——σεμνοί, πελώριοι——；——在暴风雨、洪水、瘟疫等等之中，在海的波涛里，在悬崖的威胁里，他[们]——同一个或好几个——在孩童般的知性看来显得更直接地起作用；——而孩童般的想象力把人间生活的种种事务和关系都搬到他身上去。21)

en: This childlike mind has given rise to the religious institutions and customs and representations (especially sacrifice, prayer and penance), which to reason often seem bizarre and ridiculous, often detestable — and that most of all when it sees that lust for rule has thereby deceived the good hearts of men —, always unworthy, but to the spirit and to the imagination, which puts itself back into that mind, are often lovely, often sublime, very often moving in the highest degree.

They are hallowed and propagated by tradition; besides, the interest of many men becomes so manifoldly entangled in them that the greatest degeneracy on the one hand and the progress of reason on the other are needed in order to banish, amid violent convulsions, such a system, which is woven into general habit.

The more, on one side, the spirit that originally breathed in these institutions flies away, and the holy customs and exercises then become a burden that piety did not feel before, and the more, on the other side, reason gains ground, the nearer are those customs to a sure fall. — With reason, which demands the actions of duty, there is no reconciling either the piety that brings gifts and sacrifices to the temples of the Godhead — or eases its heart in penance, mortification, fasting, long vehement prayer —, or the piety that revels in pious feelings of love, in mystical sensations.

With the progress of reason many feelings are irretrievably lost, many associations of the imagination that were once moving become weaker, which we call simplicity of morals and whose picture delights us, moves us22), whose loss we often not unjustly lament.

Traces of it, secret traits, besides those that are linked with every human inclination, every passion, where the man who wants to be wholly rational is, so to speak, often surprised at his own humanity, still always remain behind.
Why has one still in our days eagerly sought out relics of Frederick the Great, of Rousseau, and sold them dear?
zh: 宗教的设施、习俗和表象（尤其是献祭、祈祷和忏悔苦行）都出自这种孩童般的心意；在理性看来，它们往往古怪可笑，往往令人厌恶——尤其是当理性看到统治欲借此骗取了人们善良的心的时候——，总是显得不值得；但对精神和想象力来说，只要它把自己放回那种心意里去，它们就往往是可爱的，往往是崇高的，常常还动人到了极点。
它们靠传袭而变得神圣，并被一代代传下去；此外，许多人的利益又以各式各样的方式缠在里面，所以非得一方面有最大的败坏，另一方面有理性的进步，才能在剧烈的震荡中把这样一个织进了普遍习惯的体系赶出去。
一方面，最初在这些设施里呼吸的那种精神越是消散，那些神圣的习俗和功课便越成为虔敬从前感觉不到的负担；另一方面，理性越是占到地盘，那些习俗就越接近稳稳地垮掉。——理性要求的是义务的行为，跟它合不来的，既有那种把礼物和献祭送到神的庙里去、或者在忏悔苦行、克己、斋戒、长久激烈的祈祷里让心轻松一点的虔敬，也有那种在虔诚的爱的感受里、在神秘的感受里纵情享受的虔敬。
随着理性的进步，许多感受不可阻挡地失去了，许多从前动人的想象力的联想变弱了，我们把这些叫作风俗的质朴；它的画面让我们愉快、让我们感动22)，我们常常为它的失去而惋惜，并不是没有道理。
它的痕迹、隐秘的特征，总还是留了下来——除了那些跟人的每一种偏好、每一种激情连在一起的特征，在那里，一个想要完全合乎理性的人，常常会在自己的人性上仿佛被抓个正着。
为什么在我们今天，人们还那么起劲地搜寻腓特烈大帝、卢梭的遗物，并且卖得很贵？

en: It is such traits that, for example, apart from their bravery and loyalty, make the scenes of the age of chivalry so attractive to us — it is the disappearance of such associations that old age takes for the disappearance of custom itself, and that gives rise to its complaints. — When this simplicity of customs is still universal among a people, when everything is still as sacred to the princes and to the priests as to the whole people, then there is no more touching, no more beneficent spectacle — that is the happiness of the South Sea islanders, and perhaps also of the Peruvians before the quarrel of Atahualpa and Huascar.

But if an estate — the ruling one, or the priestly estate, or both at once — loses this spirit of simplicity, which founded their laws and ordinances and hitherto animated them, then it is not only gone beyond recall, but the oppression, the dishonouring, the degradation of the people is then certain (hence the division into estates is already dangerous for freedom, because there can be an esprit de corps that soon becomes contrary to the spirit of the whole).

Even if no more sacrifices, no more penances are imposed on the people than it was always accustomed to before, the whole together is yet no longer a congregation that steps jointly, unanimously in the very same sense, before the altars of its gods, but a crowd from which its leaders coax holy feelings while not feeling along with it themselves — as the juggler [coaxes] admiration from the gaping public, though he himself admires nothing, yet also does not put on an air of sharing their astonishment, whereas those others feign fellow feeling in bearing, face and words.

This contrast is then all the more outrageous to the calm spectator, the more the simplicity, the innocence of the crowd moves him; the sight of the devout people, of the eyes raised to heaven, of the folded hands, of the bent knees, of the deep sighing, of the burning prayer, would irresistibly lift his heart with pure warmth, if the principal persons of the play were not just then mixing bitterness into his feeling.
zh: 正是这类特征，比如，除了他们的勇敢和忠诚之外，还使骑士时代的一幕幕对我们如此有吸引力；——老年人把这类联想的消失当成了风俗本身的消失，他的抱怨就是由此而来的。——当一个民族还普遍保有这种风俗的淳朴，当一切对君主、对祭司来说还和对整个民族一样神圣，那就没有比这更动人、更有益的景象了——这就是南太平洋岛民的幸福，也许也是阿塔瓦尔帕和瓦斯卡尔争斗之前秘鲁人的幸福。
但如果有一个等级——统治的等级，或者教士等级，或者两者同时——失去了这种淳朴的精神，而正是这种精神创立了他们的法律和秩序、至今还在给它们注入生气，那么这种淳朴就不只是无可挽回地消失了，而且对人民的压迫、侮辱和贬低也就成了定局（所以，划分成等级对自由来说已经是危险的，因为可能出现一种团体精神，它很快就会与整体的精神相抵触）。
即使加在人民身上的献祭和忏悔苦行，并不比以前它一直习惯的更多，整个合起来也不再是一个会众——大家共同地、以同一种心意一致地走到自己神的祭坛前——，而是一群人：他们的领头人从他们身上套出神圣的感受，自己却并不一同感受——就像变戏法的从瞪大眼睛的观众那里[套出]赞叹，他自己虽然什么都不赞叹，但也不装出分享他们惊讶的样子；而那些人却在举止、表情和言语上假装有同样的感受。
这种对照，越是让平静的旁观者被民众的淳朴和无辜所打动，就越让他愤慨；虔诚的民众那一幕——望向天空的目光、合拢的双手、弯下的膝盖、深深的叹息、火热的祈祷——本来会不可抗拒地以纯粹的热情把他的心抬起来，要不是这场戏的主角们恰恰往他的感受里掺进了苦涩。

en: By what will the people recognise whether its priests have intentions in its worship other than only to increase its piety, whether its trust in them is not being abused?
zh: 人民凭什么能看出来，他的祭司在主持他的礼拜时，除了增加他的虔诚之外是否还有别的打算，他对他们的信任有没有被滥用？

en: The cause of the possibility of this degeneration lies presumably in this: that, besides the fact that the object of religion is something mysterious, most religions, especially external ones, had their secret or also generally known mysteries; that in order to be capable of being the depositary of these, particular qualities and particular preparations were needed, which gave them a distinction; and as being nearer to the sanctuary, a part of the veneration consecrated to it flowed over onto them.

They then had to make the arrangements for the religious festivals (and at every national festival religiosity presided), and the receiving and keeping or the use of the gifts for the Godhead was entrusted to their conscientiousness.
zh: 这种变质之所以可能，原因大概在于：宗教的对象本身就是某种神秘的东西，此外，大多数宗教、尤其是外在的宗教，都有自己的秘密的、或者也是众所周知的秘仪；要做这些秘仪的保管者，就得有特殊的品质、特殊的准备，这给了他们一种优越地位；而由于离圣所更近，献给圣所的那份崇敬也有一部分流到了他们身上。
于是节庆的安排就由他们来做（每一个民族节日都由宗教虔诚主持），献给神的礼物的收取、保管或使用，则交托给他们的良心。

en: A people, then, that wants to arrange its public worship in such a way that sense and imagination and the heart are touched — without reason coming away empty —, that its devotion springs from a united occupation and elevation of all the powers of the soul, and the representation of strict duty is brightened and made more accessible by beauty and cheerfulness — such a people, in order not to hand the handle of its dependence over to a class of men through its feeling, will arrange its festivals itself and use its offerings itself; and if through native institutions its sense is occupied, its power of imagination struck, its heart touched and its reason satisfied, then its spirit will feel no need — or rather it would give it no satisfaction — to lend its ears every seven days to phrases and images that were comprehensible and in place only in Syria some thousands of years ago.
zh: 那么，一个民族如果要把自己的公共礼拜安排得让感官、想象力和心都受到触动——而理性又不至于空手而回——，使它的虔诚出自灵魂一切力量的共同活动与提升，使对严格义务的表象因美和欢快而变得明朗、更容易接受，那么这样一个民族，为了不致因自己的感受而把依附的柄交到某一类人手里，就会自己安排自己的节日，自己使用自己的捐献；而如果通过本土的制度，它的感官有事可做、它的想象力受到震动、它的心受到触动、它的理性得到满足，那么它的精神就不会感到有什么需要——或者不如说，要它每七天把耳朵借给那些只在几千年前的叙利亚才可理解、才合时宜的套话和图像，它反倒不会觉得满足。

en: How little objective religion has accomplished by itself, without corresponding arrangements of the state and of the government, its history since the rise of Christianity shows us.
How little has it been able to master the corruption of all classes, the barbarism of the times, the crude prejudices of the peoples.

Opponents of the Christian religion, who with a heart full of human feeling read the history of the crusades, of the discovery of America, of the present slave trade, and not merely of these brilliant events, in which the Christian religion in part played a distinguished role, but quite generally the whole chain of princely corruption and of the depravity of the nations, and whose heart bled at it — and who then held up against this the claims of the teachers and servants of religion to excellence, to general usefulness and the like
Held declamations —, [they] had to be filled with a bitterness, with a hatred against the Christian religion, which its defenders often ascribed to a devilish malice of the heart.

Against the brilliant, horrifying pictures of the atrocities and the misery that zeal for a particular religion has stirred up — which the opponents of the Christian religion never cease to set forth with all the strength of the brush and all the sharpness of wit — its defenders object that these weapons are already too worn out and the reasons that could be drawn from them have long since been refuted; in particular, however, they give them to understand that all this calamity would not have happened if, to the good fortune of mankind, only their compendia had already been out.
zh: 客观宗教若没有国家和政府相应的设施相配合，单靠自己能做成什么，基督教产生以来的历史给我们看得很清楚。
面对一切等级的腐败、时代的野蛮、各民族粗陋的偏见，它又能制伏多少呢。
那些反对基督教的人，怀着一颗充满人的情感的心，读十字军东征的历史、发现美洲的历史、当今的奴隶买卖的历史，而且不只是这些光彩的事件——基督教在其中有一部分扮演了突出的角色——，而是根本那整整一长串君主的腐败和各民族的堕落，读的时候心都在滴血；他们又拿宗教的教师和仆人们对卓越、对普遍有用之类的诉求来与之对照，
讲出一番慷慨激昂的话——，他们就必然满心怨恨、满怀对基督教的仇恨，而它的辩护者往往把这种仇恨说成是内心魔鬼般的恶毒。
对于这些光彩夺目又令人毛骨悚然的画面——对某个特殊宗教的热忱所惹出的种种暴行和苦难——，基督教的对头们从不停手，要用尽笔力的雄浑和机智的锋利把它们摆出来；而它的辩护者则提出：这些武器已经太陈旧，从中能引出的理由早就被驳倒了；他们尤其要让对方明白，如果人类运气好、他们的教科书早就已经出来了，这一切灾祸根本就不会发生。

en: But did the popes and their cardinals, did Kukupeter [?] and the priests of his time — did they not have Moses and the prophets, could they not hear these, did these not have the pure source of morality, as we still have today — did it then need our paraphrases, our learned doctrinal concepts?
Was it incomplete in itself?

Was it not capable in itself — I will not say of improving or at least taming the morals and the coarseness of the people, but yet of having a greater influence on the class of men whose business it was their whole life long to know it and to work on themselves — was it not capable of moderating the domineering spirit of the clergy, who committed either great impudences or petty villainies, since this class of men hung up spiritual humility as a shield, since they found the reward, the commendation of these virtues, daily in the teachings of the man to whom they pretended to consecrate their whole life?
What vice has not been in circulation among them? And which of them has not been forbidden by their lord and master?
Were not the times when princes were guided by their confessors, the lands where spiritual lords ruled, the unhappiest?
zh: 可是教皇和他们的枢机主教，库库彼得[？]和他那个时代的教士，难道他们没有摩西和先知吗，难道他们不能听摩西和先知的话吗，难道他们不是和我们今天一样，手里就有道德的纯洁源头吗？——那这源头还需要我们的释义、我们那些博学的教义概念吗？
它本身是不完整的吗？
它本身难道不能——我不是说改善或者至少驯服民众的风俗和粗野，而是说对那样一类人产生更大的影响，他们一辈子的事情就是认识它、在自己身上下功夫——它难道不能约束教士阶层的专横吗？这些人要么干出极其无耻的事，要么做出卑劣的小动作，因为他们把精神上的谦卑当作盾牌挂出来，因为他们天天在那个人的教导里找到对这种美德的奖赏和称赞，而他们口口声声说要把自己的一生献给那个人。
哪一种恶习没有在他们中间流行过？可又有哪一种不是他们的主和师傅禁止过的呢？
君主由自己的告解神父牵着走的时代，教士老爷们统治的地方，不正是最不幸的时代和地方吗？

en: How light, laid in one scale of the balance, is the whole order of salvation, with the most detailed and most learned “what is that?” pressed into the head along with it, against the other scale, where all the passions, the power of circumstances, of upbringing, of examples, of government send it flying high into the air.
zh: 把整个救恩次序放到天平的一头，再把最详尽、最博学的“这是什么？”一并塞进脑子里，它比起另一头来是多么轻啊——那一头是所有情欲，是环境、教育、榜样、政府的力量，把这一头高高抛到空中。

en: As the effect and chief purpose of the Christian religion it is stated: moral improvement and being well-pleasing to God — and as the condition under which one can have the true religion, the true faith, it is demanded either that one be already so well-pleasing to God that he of himself grants one the true faith, or so morally good that one hates evil and thirsts after righteousness — i.e. through the Christian religion one can become good if one is already good beforehand.
zh: 人们说，基督教的效果和主要目的是：道德上的改善和在神面前蒙悦纳；而一个人要有真正的宗教、真正的信仰，条件则是：要么他已经那么蒙神喜悦，以致神自己就把真正的信仰赐给他，要么他已经那么道德地好，以致他憎恨恶、渴望正义——也就是说，通过基督教，一个人如果事先已经好了，就能变好。

en: Montesquieu [The Spirit of the Laws] (24, ch.
zh: 孟德斯鸠[《论法的精神》]（第24卷，第

en: “It is bad reasoning against religion to gather in a great work a long enumeration of the evils it has produced, if one does not do the same with those of the goods it has done.
If I wanted to recount all the evils that the civil laws, the monarchy, the republican government have produced in the world, I would say frightful things!”23)
zh: “在一部大著作里罗列宗教所造成的种种祸害，却不照样罗列它所造成的种种好处，这是反对宗教的拙劣推理。
如果我要讲述民法、君主制、共和制政府在世上造成过的一切祸害，我会说出骇人听闻的事情来！”23）

en: Among the commandments that Christ gave to his disciples and hearers, there are many whose observance, if it happens not in the spirit that is the spirit of virtue but only according to the letter, would be useless, often even harmful — just as the legislation of a state in which customs rule more than the laws would be very incomplete and unusable for another state in which people would allow themselves everything that is not forbidden by the laws.
Thus many commandments of Christ are contrary to the first foundations of legislation in civil societies, to the principles of the rights of property, of self-defence, etc.
A state that nowadays introduced the commandments of Christ among its people — it could do so only with the external ones, for their spirit cannot be commanded — would soon dissolve itself.

One has never yet heard that a man whose coat had been stolen and who could still save his waistcoat and trousers was scolded by a Christian teacher for not having given these up too; and in the case of the oath, in regard to which the clergy certainly knows Christ's explicit prohibition, the clergy has the most solemn role to play.
zh: 基督给他的门徒和听众的诫命中，有许多条，如果不是在美德之精神那种精神里、而只是按字句去实行，就会毫无用处，甚至常常有害——就像在一个风俗比法律更占上风的国度里，那套立法对于另一个国度会显得很不完整、没法用，因为在后一个国度里，凡是法律不禁止的事人们都敢干。
所以基督的许多诫命是和市民社会立法的首要基础、和财产权、自卫权等等的原则相抵触的。
一个国家如果今天要把基督的诫命推行到自己内部——它只能推行那些外在的诫命，因为它们的精神是命令不来的——，这个国家很快就会自己瓦解。
从来没有听说过，一个人外套被偷了、背心和裤子还保得住，会有一位基督教教师来骂他，说他不该不把这两样也一并交出去；而在起誓这件事上——教士阶层当然知道基督对此有明确的禁止——，他们却要扮演最隆重的角色。

en: What was it that above all stirred up the hatred of the scribes and the councils of the Jews against Christ? Was it not his individual manner, partly of acting himself, partly of judging the actions of other men, which offended not only against their sacred customs but also against the civil laws?

When the question was how a case was to be judged according to the legal statutes, Christ attacked the administrators of these laws; and supposing that these had been the most blameless men and wholly of his mind, they would still have had to judge not according to that, but according to the laws.
The judge must often speak otherwise than the man; the former must often condemn what the latter excuses.
zh: 主要是什么激起了文士和犹太人公会对基督的仇恨？难道不正是他那种个人的做法——一部分是自己行动，一部分是评判别人的行为——既触犯了他们神圣的习惯，也触犯了市民法律？
当问题是某个案件按司法法律该怎么判决时，基督却去攻击这些法律的执行者；就算这些人是最无可指责的人，而且完全和他同心，他们也仍然不能照他的心意，而必须照法律来判决。
法官说话常常必须和人不一样；法官常常要谴责人所以为可以原谅的事。

en: From all this it is clear that the teachings of Jesus, his principles, really suited and were directed only to the culture of individual men; e.g. when he told the young man who asks him: “Master, what shall I do to be perfect?” to sell his goods and distribute them to the poor, then the case, if one imagined it carried out as a principle of only a small congregation, of a small village, leads to consequences too absurd for one to let it occur to oneself to extend it to a larger people; or if [a congregation] unites, like the first Christians, in the midst of another people under such a law of community of goods, then the spirit of such a law has vanished precisely at the moment of the establishment itself, which through a kind of compulsion not only gives occasion to the desire for concealments, as with Ananias, [but also] restricts the beneficence of such a resignation only to its members, to the sharers of its customs and distinguishing marks, and is contrary to the spirit of the love of mankind, which pours its blessing on circumcised and uncircumcised, baptized and unbaptized.
zh: 从这一切可以看出，耶稣的学说、他的原则，本来只适合并且只着眼于个人的教养；例如，他叫那个问他“夫子，我该做什么才能完全”的青年变卖财产、分给穷人，那么这个情形，如果设想它只作为一个小教团、一个小村庄的原则来实行，就会引出太荒唐的后果，谁也不会想到把它推及一个更大的民族；或者，如果一个[教团]像最初的基督徒那样，在另一个民族中间按这样一条财产共有的法则结合起来，那么这样一条法则的精神恰恰在建立的那一刻就已经消失了：这种建立通过某种强制，不但引起隐瞒的心思，像亚拿尼亚那样，[而且]把这样一种放弃的善行只限制在自己的成员身上，限制在那些与自己有同样习俗和标记的同伴身上，并且违背人类之爱的精神，这种爱把祝福倾洒在受割礼的和未受割礼的、受洗的和未受洗的人身上。

en: ... public power, which presumes to press into the sanctuary of the heart, where only the friend is voluntarily admitted — now it proceeds to an explanation of the intentions, which are artificially pieced together out of circumstances.
zh: ……公共权力，竟擅自挤进心灵的圣所，而那里只有朋友才被自愿准许进入——现在它开始解释那些意图，而这些意图是从各种情况里拼凑出来的。

en: The presumption of testing hearts and reins and of judging and punishing consciences, which crept in gradually and could easily creep in, since the seed of it already lay in the first origin of Christianity, since what only concerns a small family was falsely extended to civil society — this presumption, which established itself in an incredible way — for it ought to seem incredible that men should so far forget their rights and feel this loss so little — has occasioned the most outrageous outgrowths, of violent institutions and delusions of mankind: auricular confession, excommunication, penances, and the whole sequence of these dishonouring monuments to the degradation of mankind.

The Reformers, who in their doctrinal propositions wanted to follow the utterances of the New Testament, who in their Christian police-institutions — for without such they did not believe that an exercise of religion [could] take place; for to set up a church power as a support of freedom of conscience, as a counterweight to princely power, they did not think of, for they subjected Christianity to the secular power — wanted in church policing to follow the simplicity of the first church, were thereby misled into overlooking the difference between the necessary institutions of a dominant folk religion and the private laws of a partial society, a club — how could they have torn themselves away from the concept of a church as a kind of status in statu, from a visible, uniform community and union for a determinate ritus?

How far, for example, Luther was from the idea of the worship of God in spirit and in truth is shown by his sad quarrels with Zwingli, Oecolampadius, etc.; he took from the clergy the power to rule by violence and over the purses, but he still wanted it over opinions.

The princes, with their court chaplains, as the guardians of their people, gave their children tutors who were to lead them in leading-strings, admonish them, and in case of need also chastise them with the rod.

Hence the church punishments were retained besides the political ones, the church penances and the like, hence the confessions, the actual auricular confession [indeed] set aside, but the clergy retained as confessors, in order to come to the aid of the troubled consciences, whose imagination one incessantly assailed and first made anxious; in that one traced religion back to improvement of the heart, repentance and conversion, but did not stop at these general expressions of a state, which in the heart of every man are really something different, different according to temperament, inclination and imagination, but dissected the states in this way, thus engaged in playthings of feelings; — since one presented these states as something tangible or falling into the senses, whose arrival or presence one could know as well as one can look at the clock whether it is twelve; — since one [gave] detailed psychological description of these states, as if they were the same in all men, which therefore were anyway artificially fitted into one another and ordered one after another, not according to a real knowledge of the human heart, but according to theological prejudices about an innate corruption of human nature, by a ridiculous exegesis accompanied by no knowledge of men; — since all this was thus incessantly pounded or dandled into the memory and conscience of the common man, such a sour-sweet dough necessarily had to ruin his healthy, strong, active juices — countless misunderstandings with his own inclinations and stirrings had to arise, such a disorganised anxiousness of conscience had to arise, that in place of a fullness of feelings there had to step insipid sentimentality, an undigested word-jumble, [in place of] energy, confidence in oneself, respect for oneself a hypocritical humility, a spiritual vanity, which is always busy with itself and its stirrings and knows how to chatter endlessly about its feelings, victories, anxious assaults, and has to do with them; — now indeed the clergy had their hands full of resolving doubts, strengthening against assaults, warning against secret influences of evil, comforting in sufferings which the world, the assaults of Satan and one's own evil lusts and desires bring forth — they are patients who cannot bear healthy air and fresh water, but now live on insipid broths and the apothecary's mixtures, keep a diary about every wind that presses their entrails, every sneeze and clearing of the throat, and otherwise have to do with no one but themselves, at most present their tisanes to the petitioner and commend him to the care of God.

One can see it in the theological compendia, where it is not really knowledge of religion [but] what is only knowledge of the psychological course or of the manner of producing certain states of soul that makes up the main part — in accordance with the principle that repentance and conversion are really the most important thing, to which, however, one is led by the most unexpected detours, where it is then no wonder if one loses oneself in these too much to reach the actual firm goal; this thought of improvement and of the way to it is spun out so, divided into so many stations, equipped with so many foreign names, which express one and the same thing — but through their strangeness and difference seem to hold wondrous secrets and important matters in themselves, from the gratia applicatrix to the unio mystica — that one no longer recognises the simplest things in it, and, if one looks at the things with healthy eyes in the light, must be ashamed that all this art and learning is expended on a matter which common human understanding grasps in a quarter of an hour; nowadays one has found that subjective religion cannot be forced into dogmatics, and the objective now takes up the main part of it, doctrines which, if not always for reason, at least entertain the memory and the understanding.

This church discipline of the Christians is not something that was newly entered into the statutes of Christian society only after its emergence, but it is, as we have seen, already contained in its first undeveloped draft and was then used and extended by lust for power and hypocrisy.

However much the traces of its crudest abuse are beginning to disappear, there is still infinitely much of its spirit left behind, and it gives us a new example among the many, that institutions, laws of a small society, where every citizen [has] the freedom to be a member or not, when they are extended to the great civil society, are never appropriate and cannot exist together with civil freedom.
zh: 那种检验人的心肠肺腑、审判并惩罚良心的自负，是渐渐混进来的，而且很容易混进来，因为基督教的源头里就已经有了它的种子，因为本来只关系到一个大家庭的事被错误地推广到了市民社会——这种自负以令人难以置信的方式扎下了根——因为人竟然这样忘掉自己的权利、对这样的丧失又这样无动于衷，本该显得难以置信——它引发了最令人愤慨的过度做法，引发了对人类的暴力制度与蒙蔽：耳语告解、逐出教会、赎罪苦修，以及这一连串使人蒙羞的、人类被贬低的纪念物。

宗教改革家们在教义上想遵循《新约》的说法，在他们的基督教治安制度上——因为没有这样的制度，他们就不相信宗教的实践[能够]进行；至于把一种教会权力立为良心自由的支柱、用来制衡诸侯的权力，他们根本就没有想到，因为他们把基督教交给了世俗权力——在教会治安上想效法最初教会的单纯，他们因此被引入迷途，忽略了在一种占主导地位的民间宗教所必需的制度同一个局部团体、一个俱乐部的私人法则之间的区别——他们又怎么能挣脱这样一种教会的概念：教会是一种 status in statu（国中之国），是一个可见的、整齐划一的共同体，是为了某种确定仪式的联合？
例如，路德离在精神和真理中敬拜上帝的观念有多远，从他与茨温利、厄科兰帕迪乌斯等人那些可悲的争吵就可以看出：他剥夺了教士用暴力、用钱袋来进行统治的权力，但他还想统治人们的意见。
诸侯们带着他们的宫廷教士，作为自己人民的监护人，给自己的孩子请了家庭教师，让他们牵着孩子走、时时告诫，必要时还用鞭子责打。

因此，除了政治性的惩罚，教会的惩罚、教会赎罪之类也保留了下来，因此忏悔保留了：现实的耳语告解[虽然]取消了，但教士作为听忏悔的神父保留下来，去帮助那些不安的良心——人们不断地攻打他们的想象力，先使他们害怕起来；人们把宗教归结为心的改善、悔改和皈依，却不满足于这些关于某种状态的一般说法——这些状态在每个人心里其实都是不同的东西，随气质、爱好和想象力而各不相同——而是把这些状态这样细细拆解，这样沉溺于感受的小把戏；——人们把这些状态说成是某种可以摸到、可以感觉到的东西，它们的到来或存在，人们能像看钟表知道是不是十二点一样清楚地知道；——人们[给出]对这些状态的详细心理学描述，好像它们在所有人身上都一样，而这些描述本来就不是根据对人的心的真正认识，而是根据神学偏见，即人性天生败坏，靠一种毫无人情世故的、可笑的解经法人工拼凑起来、前后排列起来；——既然这一切被这样不停地砸进或逗弄进普通人的记忆和良心里，那么这样一种又酸又甜的面团就必然要败坏他那健康、有力、活跃的汁液——必然产生无数与他自己的爱好、冲动的误解，必然产生这样一种紊乱的良心上的恐惧，以致代替丰富感受的，是乏味的感伤、一堆没消化的空话，[代替]行动的力量、自信和自我尊重，则是虚伪的谦卑、一种宗教的虚荣，它总是忙着和自己以及自己的各种情绪打交道，能无穷无尽地絮叨自己的感受、胜利、惶恐的试探，并且以此为业；——现在教士们当然忙得不可开交：要解决怀疑，要在试探中给人以力量，要警告人提防恶的隐秘影响，要在世界、撒旦的试探和自己邪恶的情欲贪欲所造成的苦难中给人安慰——这些人是病人，受不了健康的空气和清水，如今靠乏味的汤药和药剂师的混合药活着，对每一阵压迫他们内脏的风、每一个喷嚏和每一声清嗓子都记一本日记，除此之外不再和任何人打交道，只和自己打交道，顶多把他们的汤药端给来求他们的人，把他托付给上帝的看顾。

从神学手册上就可以看出：其中占主要部分的其实不是宗教的认识，[而是]那种只算认识心理过程、认识如何造出某些灵魂状态的知识——这符合这样一条原则：悔改和皈依本来是最重要的，可是偏要绕最意想不到的弯路把人引到那里去，于是一个人在这上面陷得太深、反而到不了真正确定的目标，也就不足为奇了；这种改善以及通往改善之路的想法被拉得这样长，分成这么多站，配上这么多外来的名称——它们表达的是同一件事，却靠自己的陌生和差异，好像里面藏着什么奇妙的秘密和了不起的东西，从 gratia applicatrix（应用的恩典）一直到 unio mystica（神秘合一）——以致人们再也认不出其中最简单的事情，而当人们用健康的眼睛在光下看这些事情时，不得不羞愧：所有这些技巧和学问，都用在一件普通人的健全理智一刻钟就能明白的事情上；如今人们发现，主观的宗教没法硬塞进教义学，而客观的东西现在占了教义学的主要部分，那些学说即使并不总是为了理性，至少也让记忆和知性有事可做。
基督徒的这种教会管教并不是它产生之后才新写进基督教团体章程里的东西，而是像我们看到的，在它最初尚未展开的草稿里就已经包含着了，后来被专横的统治欲和虚伪加以利用和扩张。
尽管它最粗野的滥用的痕迹已开始消失，它的精神却还有无穷无尽的东西留了下来，而且它给我们提供了一个新的例子，加入到那许多例子中去：一个小团体的制度和法则，在那里每个公民[都有]做成员或不做成员的自由，一旦被推广到大的市民社会，就绝不合宜，也不能和市民自由并存。

en: Thus in a state where not every citizen is the natural defender of his fatherland, but where there are nevertheless enough volunteers who take this office upon themselves for some money, a society can bind itself to one another never to take weapons in hand, never to take part in wars whose legitimacy it knows as little as the advantages, if the state in which they live remains victor; which in general believes itself entitled in no case to go out to the murder of other men, and opposes individual acts of violence only with patience and submission.

But if such a society itself grew into a state, it can no longer maintain its maxims in their universality, if it does not want to run the risk of surrendering, with the suppression of all natural feeling, its whole edifice of the happiness of the entire people to the insolence of a handful of robbers.
zh: 因此，在一个并非每个公民都是自己祖国天然保卫者、却又有足够多的志愿兵为了一点钱就承担起这个职务的国家里，一个团体可以互相约定：绝不拿起武器，绝不参加战争，因为他们对战争是否正当知道得并不比——万一他们所在的那个国家打了胜仗——对自己有什么好处知道得更多；这个团体总之在任何情况下都认为自己无权去杀害别人，对个别的暴力行为只用忍耐和顺从来对付。
但如果这样一个团体自己长成了一个国家，它就再也不能保持它那些原则的普遍性了，除非它甘愿冒这样的险：压制一切自然感情，把整个民族的幸福这座大厦拱手交给一小撮强盗的放肆。

en: Just as the best education of children is the good example that they see around them daily, and just as they become the more inclined to disobedience and sullen obstinacy the more one always has to command them, so it is also with the education of man on the large scale.

They withdraw from, they shun (ils ne se prêtent pas, ils se refusent) a religion that wants to keep them in leading-strings forever and ever, that chatters down to them about a multitude of virtues and vices which they have never in life seen in the abstract as one here describes them, or which are not at all suited to human situations.
All the more, without their knowing it themselves, [it] has a secret influence on them; even the freest man stands in dependence on the spirit of the men who surround him.

He who otherwise would be least tolerant of fault-finding — when in general a virtue or repentance and conversion in general is recommended from the pulpits, everyone already accepts that, everyone lets it be said to him, because it concerns all no less than him.

But if a detailed, faithful picture is made of prevailing corruptions, if individual traits are woven in, then this works in him who feels hit, who feels his property, his way of acting attacked, rather as bitterness; he holds no authority entitled to presume such a thing.

(Children are guided by mere sensuousness, by love and fear — the grown man is besides also capable of being guided by reason; at least he hardly does, like the child, what is for his own best only to please others, out of love for someone, without first seeing that it is good.) — Everyone finds it unbearable when strangers meddle in his affairs, especially in his way of acting; most unbearable are publicly set-up moral watchmen.
He who acts with a sincere heart is first misunderstood by the people with the moral and religious ruler.
zh: 正如对孩子最好的教育就是他们每天在身边看到的好榜样，也正如人们越是老要命令他们，他们就越容易不听话、闹别扭，对人类的大规模教育也是如此。
他们躲开、回避（ils ne se prêtent pas, ils se refusent）这样一种宗教：它老是要牵着他们走，成天向他们唠叨一大堆美德和恶习，而他们在生活中从来没有像这里描述的那样抽象地见过这些，或者这些美德恶习根本不适合人的实际处境。
正因为如此，[它]在他们自己不知道的情况下对他们有一种隐秘的影响；哪怕最自由的人，也依赖周围人的精神。
平常最受不了别人挑刺的人——当讲道台上一般地劝人要有某种美德，或者一般地劝人悔改皈依时，每个人都会接受，每个人都让人对自己这样说，因为这事关系到所有人，并不比关系到他少。
但如果把盛行的败坏画成一幅详细而忠实的图画，再织入一些个别的特征，那么这在一个觉得自己被击中、觉得自己的财产、自己的做法受到攻击的人身上，引起的更多是恼怒；他认为没有任何权威有权做这种事。
（孩子只靠感性、靠爱和怕来引导——而成年人除此之外还有能力接受理性的引导；至少他不会像孩子那样，仅仅为了讨别人喜欢、出于对某人的爱，去做对自己最好的事，而不先看出它是好的。）——人人都觉得受不了外人插手自己的事，尤其是自己的做法；最让人受不了的是公开设岗的道德纠察。
用心纯正行事的人，最容易受到那些拿着道德和宗教尺子的人误解。
